BAWAL ANG “MARCOS RESIGN” SA TRILLION PESO MARCH RALLY?

Mahigpit na ipinagbabawal umano ang panawagan na patalsikin si Marcos Jr. sa gaganaping “Trillion Peso March” sa EDSA People Power Monument sa Pebrero 25.

Ayon kay KiKo Dee, co-convenor ng Tindig Pilipinas, malinaw na hindi papayagan ang anumang panawagan na naglalayong pabagsakin ang isang halal na opisyal o magpanukala ng kapalit sa puwesto.

Giit ni Dee, labag umano sa Konstitusyon ang direktang panawagan ng pagpapatalsik sa isang pangulo nang hindi dumadaan sa tamang proseso ng batas.

Nilinaw rin ng grupo na ang layunin ng Trillion Peso March ay ipahayag ang sentimyento ng publiko laban sa umano’y mga isyu sa paggastos ng pondo ng gobyerno, at hindi upang itulak ang destabilization o pagbabago ng pamahalaan sa labas ng legal na paraan.

#marcos #duterte #VPSaraDuterte #DavaoCity #AngBalitaNgayonFB

Organizers of “EDSA 40: Tuloy ang Laban sa Korapsyon at Kahirapan” meet with Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III, along with representatives from national and local agencies, at the EDSA People Power Monument in Quezon City on Friday, Feb. 20, to discuss preparations for the 40th anniversary of the People Power Revolution on Feb. 25.

The meeting focuses on assessing traffic flow, security measures, and crowd management to ensure public safety and smooth coordination during the event.

📷: Santi San Juan | MB

IN PHOTOS │Members of GABRIELA stage a Black Friday protest calling for the removal of the 12% Value-Added Tax (VAT) on electricity, arguing that the levy worsens the burden of rising power costs on poor households. Demonstrators tore electricity bills from Meralco to denounce what they described as a “double hold-up” — soaring power rates and the VAT — which they claim inflates basic expenses while public funds are allegedly lost to corruption.

data.text:
Members of the Working People Against Corruption (WPAC), a broad alliance of workers’ groups and unions, stage a Black Friday protest at Isetann Recto along Recto Avenue in Manila on Feb. 20.

Carrying placards bearing the call “Mga Kurakot, Panagutin! Sahod Pataasin!”, the group demands accountability over alleged government corruption and pushes for higher wages for workers.

The protest is part of the alliance’s continuing campaign against corruption across various sectors and industries. It also forms part of the buildup activities of the EDSA@40 coalition ahead of the 40th anniversary of the EDSA People Power Revolution. 

📷: Mark Balmores | MB
